gen-eater-gf-fragment-mono: Fragment Mono lays its letters out like nails on a ruler, each one marching at the same pace beneath Eater's spiky display heading. Fragment Mono keeps a monospace page moving smoothly, since no thick-and-thin swings slow the eye.
gen-eater-gf-genos: Eater looks dark and aggressive, with wide gaps between its letters. Genos tucks its sans-serif glyphs so close their edges almost touch, and that tight, clean texture is the strongest thing the pair has going.
gen-eater-gf-geom: Thin strokes that are clearly thinner yet never fragile give Eater its dark, aggressive bite. Geom comes in with a lofty lowercase band and a friendly manner, and that gap in temperament is the pair's best quality.
gen-eater-gf-hammersmith-one: Eater's thin strokes are clearly lighter than its stems, though the contrast stays mild and never turns brittle. Hammersmith One replies with rounded strokes like cut lengths of cord, so the heading's menace gets a soft, even landing below.
gen-eater-gf-inder: Inder reads clean and businesslike, with little height difference between its capitals and lowercase. Inder sits quietly under Eater, whose headline words shimmer with shifting weight and wide gaps between letters.
gen-eater-gf-jaldi: Dark and aggressive, Eater lets a subtle gradient of weight run along every curve. Jaldi follows with a x-height pushed well above the usual, brushed-on letters and a visibly gaping c, so the sans-serif text feels roomy beside that menace.
gen-eater-gf-menbere: Menbere stacks its lowercase high like rolled cord, which gives its sans text a clean, upright stance. Eater's heading moves more, with weight shifting along each stroke.
gen-eater-gf-mukta: Eater brings moderate thick-thin transitions and short ascenders, all dark and aggressive. Mukta answers with tall-bodied small letters in sans-serif, and that steady, clean text against the heading's menace is what makes the pair work.
gen-eater-gf-mukta-mahee: Mukta Mahee sets chunky, lofty lowercase letters that feel approachable and clean. Mukta Mahee would crowd the heading if made large, though, since Eater's in-between stroke contrast needs the room to stay menacing.
gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-display: Spiky and dark, Eater spaces its letters wide and keeps its ascenders short against the body height. Noto Sans Display gives every word a big middle zone, and that friendly bulk is the pair's strongest card.
